findings.title: Missing CSRF protection on state-changing operations
findings.description: The application uses FastAPI with CORS middleware allowing credentials but does not implement CSRF token validation. POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints for user/item management lack CSRF protection, making the application vulnerable to cross-site request forgery attacks from malicious websites.

locations.snippet:
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=settings.all_cors_origins,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection by: 1) Adding CsrfMiddleware or custom CSRF token validation, 2) Requiring CSRF tokens in POST/PUT/DELETE requests, 3) Setting SameSite=Strict on session cookies, 4) Restricting allow_methods to specific HTTP methods instead of '*'

findings.title: Insufficient JWT token validation strictness
findings.description: JWT tokens are accepted from localStorage without strict validation of token claims. The frontend retrieves tokens from localStorage synchronously without validating token expiration client-side before use. If a token expires, it will only be caught after the API request fails, allowing brief window for token replay or use of expired tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add JWT token expiration validation: 1) Decode JWT client-side using a library like jwt-decode to check exp claim, 2) Compare token expiration with current time before API calls, 3) Proactively refresh or clear expired tokens from localStorage, 4) Implement token refresh endpoint that returns new access token with refresh token rotation

findings.title: Access token stored in localStorage is vulnerable to XSS
findings.description: JWT access tokens are stored in browser localStorage, which is vulnerable to XSS attacks. Any XSS vulnerability in the application or third-party scripts could steal the token. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running in the page context.
findings.suggested_fix: Migrate token storage to secure, HttpOnly cookies: 1) Backend should set access token in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies instead of returning it to frontend, 2) Remove localStorage access token storage, 3) Configure OpenAPI client to use cookie-based auth automatically, 4) Implement XSRF-TOKEN cookie for CSRF protection alongside HttpOnly auth cookie

findings.title: Missing authorization checks on /api/utils/health-check endpoint
findings.description: The health-check endpoint used by Docker healthcheck is not shown in auth_boundaries but is referenced in compose.yml. If unprotected, it could allow unauthenticated users to probe API availability, potentially enabling reconnaissance attacks.

locations.snippet:
healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/api/v1/utils/health-check/"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that /api/v1/utils/health-check/ is intentionally public for monitoring purposes. If it should be private, add authentication requirement. If public is intended, ensure it returns minimal information and doesn't expose version/system details that could aid attackers.

findings.title: Password reset token lacks expiration validation
findings.description: The password reset token validation in verify_password_reset_token() does not enforce token expiration. While tokens are likely issued with expiration, if validation is lenient or missing, attackers could use old/captured reset tokens indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that verify_password_reset_token() in backend/app/utils.py: 1) Validates token expiration timestamp, 2) Rejects tokens older than acceptable threshold (e.g., 24 hours), 3) Returns None for expired tokens, 4) Consider one-time use tokens stored in database that are deleted after use, 5) Add token creation timestamp to response for audit logging

findings.title: No rate limiting on authentication endpoints
findings.description: Login endpoint (/login/access-token) and password recovery endpoints (/password-recovery/{email}) lack rate limiting. Attackers can perform brute force attacks on user credentials or enumerate registered emails without throttling.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting middleware: 1) Use slowapi or similar FastAPI rate limiting library, 2) Limit login attempts to 5 per minute per IP, 3) Limit password recovery to 3 per hour per email, 4) Consider exponential backoff after threshold exceeded, 5) Log failed attempts for security monitoring, 6) Return generic error messages to prevent username enumeration timing attacks

findings.title: Session management lacks explicit logout/token revocation
findings.description: Logout removes token from localStorage but there is no server-side token revocation mechanism. An attacker with a stolen token can still use it until natural expiration. There is no token blacklist or revocation endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement server-side token revocation: 1) Create /api/logout endpoint that accepts token and adds to blacklist, 2) Store revoked tokens in Redis with expiration matching token TTL, 3) Check blacklist on every API request before processing, 4) Call logout endpoint from frontend before clearing localStorage, 5) Implement token refresh endpoint to enable short-lived access tokens with longer-lived refresh tokens

findings.title: Admin endpoint lacks proper superuser verification
findings.description: The admin routes are protected but the access control may rely solely on is_superuser check without additional verification. No multi-factor authentication or additional confirmation for sensitive admin operations.

locations.snippet: (File content not provided, but referenced in auth_boundaries as /api/users requiring jwt auth)

findings.suggested_fix: Strengthen admin authorization: 1) Verify get_current_active_superuser dependency is properly checking is_superuser AND is_active, 2) Log all admin operations with timestamp and user ID, 3) Consider requiring email confirmation before sensitive admin operations (user deletion, permission changes), 4) Implement admin action audit log with immutable records, 5) For highly sensitive operations, require re-authentication

findings.title: No verification of email ownership for user registration
findings.description: User signup endpoint allows registration without email verification. The is_verified field is set during initial_data.py but not enforced during registration flow. Attackers could register with fake emails or others' emails.

locations.snippet: (File not fully shown but registration creates users without email verification)

findings.suggested_fix: Implement email verification: 1) Send verification email on signup with time-limited token, 2) Mark user as is_verified=false initially, 3) Require email verification before account activation, 4) Prevent login for unverified users or restrict functionality, 5) Resend verification email endpoint with rate limiting, 6) Verification token should be single-use and expire after 24 hours

findings.title: Passwords transmitted over HTTPS but no additional encryption layer
findings.description: Password fields are sent as plain text in HTTPS POST requests. While HTTPS provides transport security, there is no field-level encryption or PBKDF2/additional hashing during transmission.
findings.suggested_fix: While HTTPS is primary defense, consider: 1) Ensure TLS 1.2+ is enforced (verify in Traefik config), 2) Use strong cipher suites only, 3) Implement HSTS header, 4) Consider bcrypt key derivation on client before sending (though server should still hash), 5) Verify certificate pinning in production, 6) Add Content-Security-Policy headers to prevent man-in-the-middle

findings.title: No protection against credential stuffing with known password lists
findings.description: Login endpoint accepts any password without checking against common password lists or breach databases. Users with weak/common passwords are vulnerable to credential stuffing attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement password validation against breach databases: 1) On signup/password change, validate against HaveIBeenPwned API or local password list, 2) Reject passwords that appear in top 100k most common passwords, 3) Enforce minimum password requirements (12+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols), 4) Implement progressive password strength meter on frontend, 5) Add rate limiting specifically for wrong password attempts to prevent brute force

findings.title: Insufficient protection against horizontal privilege escalation
findings.description: Users can potentially access other users' data through predictable ID enumeration in /api/users/{id} endpoint. No ownership verification shown before returning user details.

locations.snippet: (File not fully shown, but users endpoint requires jwt auth without shown ownership checks)

findings.suggested_fix: Implement proper ownership verification: 1) In read_user endpoint, verify current_user.id == requested_user.id unless current_user.is_superuser, 2) Return 404 instead of 403 for non-existent or unauthorized resources to prevent enumeration, 3) Add audit logging for all user data access attempts, 4) For items endpoint, verify item.owner_id == current_user.id before returning, 5) Implement field-level authorization to hide sensitive data

findings.title: No account lockout after failed login attempts
findings.description: Failed login attempts are not tracked. After multiple failed attempts, account should be temporarily locked to prevent brute force attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement account lockout mechanism: 1) Track failed login attempts in Redis or database with user_id/email key, 2) Increment counter on authentication failure, 3) Lock account temporarily after 5 failed attempts (15-30 min lockout), 4) Send email notification on account lockout, 5) Provide admin unlock and user self-unlock via email, 6) Reset counter on successful login, 7) Log all lockout events for security monitoring

findings.title: Missing security headers in responses
findings.description: FastAPI application does not appear to set security headers like HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy. These headers provide browser-level security protections.

locations.snippet:
app = FastAPI(
    title=settings.PROJECT_NAME,
    openapi_url=f"{settings.API_V1_STR}/openapi.json",
    generate_unique_id_function=custom_generate_unique_id,
)

if settings.all_cors_origins:
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=settings.all_cors_origins,
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )

findings.suggested_fix: Add security middleware to FastAPI: 1) Add middleware to set Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, 2) Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, 3) Set X-Frame-Options: DENY, 4) Set X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block, 5) Add Content-Security-Policy header, 6) Set Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, 7) Consider using starlette.middleware.secureheaders or TrustedHostMiddleware

findings.title: Password stored without verification of adequate hashing algorithm
findings.description: While code references Argon2 and bcrypt upgrade logic, the actual password hashing in backend/app/core/security.py is not shown. Cannot verify that hashing is using strong parameters (adequate memory, iterations) and not using deprecated algorithms.

locations.snippet:
def test_login_with_bcrypt_password_upgrades_to_argon2(
    client: TestClient, db: Session
) -> None:
    """Test that logging in with a bcrypt password hash upgrades it to argon2."""
    email = random_email()
    password = random_lower_string()

    # Create a bcrypt hash directly (simulating legacy password)
    bcrypt_hasher = BcryptHasher()
    bcrypt_hash = bcrypt_hasher.hash(password)
    assert bcrypt_hash.startswith("$2")  # bcrypt hashes start with $2

findings.suggested_fix: Verify password hashing security: 1) Ensure backend/app/core/security.py uses pwdlib with Argon2 as default with settings: time_cost=2, memory_cost=19 (minimum), 2) Verify verify_password function is using constant-time comparison, 3) Ensure password reset tokens are generated with secrets.token_urlsafe(32), 4) Verify hashed passwords are stored with salt and algorithm identifier, 5) Document password hashing parameters in configuration

findings.title: Hard-coded pagination limit of 100 in users endpoint
findings.description: The read_users endpoint has a hard-coded default limit of 100 without a maximum limit validation. While pagination is implemented, there's no upper bound check which could allow clients to request very large result sets.

locations.snippet: def read_users(session: SessionDep, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> Any:

findings.suggested_fix: Add validation to cap the limit: `limit = min(limit, 100)` to prevent excessive data retrieval.

findings.title: Hard-coded pagination limit of 100 in items endpoint
findings.description: The read_items endpoint has a hard-coded default limit of 100 without a maximum limit validation, similar to users endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add validation to cap the limit: `limit = min(limit, 100)` to prevent excessive data retrieval.

findings.title: Duplicate database queries for count and data in users endpoint
findings.description: The read_users endpoint executes two separate database queries - one for count and one for data. While acceptable for small datasets, this could be optimized using a window function or cached count.

locations.snippet:
count_statement = select(func.count()).select_from(User)
    count = session.exec(count_statement).one()

    statement = (
        select(User).order_by(col(User.created_at).desc()).offset(skip).limit(limit)
    )
    users = session.exec(statement).all()

findings.suggested_fix: Consider using a single query with window function or accepting that for pagination this pattern is common and acceptable. The current implementation is a reasonable trade-off.

findings.title: Missing response caching in API client
findings.description: The frontend API client (axios-based) has no caching mechanism. Each API call hits the server even if the same data was recently fetched.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement a caching layer using React Query (already installed via @tanstack/react-query) or implement a simple in-memory cache for GET requests. Configure queryClient with default caching options.

findings.title: SDK generation prevents tree-shaking
findings.description: The OpenAPI SDK generation is configured with `asClass: true` which prevents tree-shaking, causing larger bundle sizes as all generated code is included regardless of usage.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `asClass: true` to enable tree-shaking, or use the function-based API which allows better dead code elimination. The comment explicitly acknowledges this limitation.

findings.title: Missing lazy loading for route components
findings.description: The TanStack Router configuration doesn't use lazy loading for route components. All route components are bundled together, increasing initial load time.
findings.suggested_fix: Use React.lazy() and Suspense for route components: `const AdminPage = React.lazy(() => import("./_layout/admin"))`

findings.title: Axios instance recreated on each request
findings.description: The request function creates axiosClient from the default axios import each time, rather than reusing a configured instance.

locations.snippet: export const request = <T>(config: OpenAPIConfig, options: ApiRequestOptions<T>, axiosClient: AxiosInstance = axios): CancelablePromise<T> => {

findings.suggested_fix: Create a singleton axios instance with default config (base URL, interceptors, timeout) and reuse it across all requests.

findings.title: No database query result caching
findings.description: The backend doesn't implement any query result caching. Repeated identical queries (e.g., listing users/items) hit the database every time.

locations.snippet:
def read_users(session: SessionDep, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> Any:
    """
    Retrieve users.
    """

    count_statement = select(func.count()).select_from(User)
    count = session.exec(count_statement).one()

    statement = (
        select(User).order_by(col(User.created_at).desc()).offset(skip).limit(limit)
    )
    users = session.exec(statement).all()

findings.suggested_fix: Consider implementing Redis-based caching for frequently accessed, rarely changing data like user listings. Use cache invalidation on mutations.

findings.description: Database connection pooling configuration is not explicitly visible in the provided code. The default SQLAlchemy connection pool settings may not be optimal for production workloads.

findings.title: Backend API module lacks service layer abstraction
findings.description: The backend-api module (800 LOC) directly imports and uses CRUD operations from backend-models, creating tight coupling between routes and data access layer. Business logic is intermingled with HTTP request handling, violating separation of concerns. Routes in users.py, items.py, and login.py directly instantiate database sessions and call CRUD functions without a domain service layer to coordinate operations.

locations.snippet: Routes directly call crud.get_user, crud.create_user without service coordination
Auth logic mixed with route handlers, direct DB access in route context
Item CRUD operations called directly from route handlers

findings.suggested_fix: Create service layer (e.g., UserService, ItemService, AuthService) in a new backend/app/services/ module. Move business logic, validation, and cross-cutting concerns into services. Routes should only handle HTTP concerns (request/response transformation) and delegate to services. This decouples routes from data layer and enables easier testing and reuse.

findings.title: Frontend components module is a god module with mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The frontend-components module (2500 LOC across 51 files) mixes UI presentation, business logic, API calls, and form handling in individual component files. Admin components (AddUser.tsx, EditUser.tsx) contain form validation, API mutations, and toast notifications. Items components do similar pattern. This violates single responsibility and makes components hard to test and reuse. No clear separation between container (smart) and presentational (dumb) components.

locations.snippet: Component combines form rendering, validation logic, API call handling, and state management
Similar pattern: form UI + business logic + API integration + error handling
Item addition logic tightly coupled with React component

findings.suggested_fix: Refactor components into: (1) Presentational components (UI only, no business logic), (2) Custom hooks for data fetching/mutations (useAddUser, useEditUser), (3) Custom hooks for form handling (useUserForm), (4) Container components that orchestrate hooks and pass props to presentational components. Extract validation logic into separate utility functions. Consider moving API-related logic to React Query mutation definitions in a hooks directory.

findings.title: Missing abstraction between frontend routes and components
findings.description: Frontend route files (_layout/admin.tsx, _layout/items.tsx) directly render components that contain business logic and API calls. No proper page/container component pattern exists. Routes are tightly coupled to specific component implementations, making it difficult to swap implementations or create variations.

locations.snippet: Route directly uses Admin/Items components
Route directly uses Items components

findings.suggested_fix: Create container/page components (e.g., AdminPage.tsx, ItemsPage.tsx) in a new frontend/src/pages/ directory. These containers orchestrate data fetching, state management, and component composition. Routes should reference page components, which then compose presentational components. This adds a clear abstraction layer and makes routes simpler.

findings.title: Inconsistent client SDK usage across frontend
findings.description: The frontend-client module (450 LOC) provides generated OpenAPI client (sdk.gen.ts), but there's no consistent pattern for how components use it. Some components likely use openapi-fetch directly, others may use React Query with the client, creating inconsistent patterns. No centralized API client configuration or wrapper exists to standardize error handling, interceptors, or request/response transformation.

locations.snippet: Generated client with no wrapper pattern visible in architecture
Core API configuration with no consistent usage pattern across components

findings.suggested_fix: Create a custom API client hook or service wrapper (e.g., frontend/src/services/api.ts) that standardizes how the generated SDK is used. Define React Query hooks that wrap SDK calls with consistent error handling, loading states, and caching strategies. Document the pattern in a frontend API layer convention document.

findings.title: Backend models module mixes concerns: ORM models, CRUD, and utilities
findings.description: The backend-models module (600 LOC across 6 files) combines SQLAlchemy ORM definitions (models.py), CRUD operations (crud.py), general utilities (utils.py), data initialization (initial_data.py), and pre-start scripts in the root backend/app/ directory. This creates a dumping ground for loosely related code. Models should be separate from CRUD operations and utilities should be organized by domain.

locations.snippet: ORM model definitions
CRUD operations mixed with models in single directory
Miscellaneous utilities scattered in root

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize backend/app/ to: (1) backend/app/schemas/ - Pydantic request/response schemas, (2) backend/app/models/ - SQLAlchemy ORM models organized by domain, (3) backend/app/repositories/ - CRUD operations (repository pattern), (4) backend/app/utils/ - utilities organized by function (date_utils.py, validation_utils.py), (5) backend/app/services/ - business logic layer. Consider placing pre-start scripts in backend/app/scripts/.

findings.title: Tight coupling between backend routes and dependency injection
findings.description: Backend routes depend on deps.py for injecting database sessions and current user. While FastAPI's dependency injection is a valid pattern, there's no abstraction for testability. The deps.py module (57 LOC) directly creates database sessions and validates tokens, but routes depend on specific dependency signatures. Changes to dependency resolution require updating route signatures.

locations.snippet: Dependency injection functions tightly coupled to route signatures
Routes import and depend on specific deps signatures

findings.suggested_fix: Create an abstraction layer for dependencies (e.g., backend/app/api/dependencies.py or backend/app/di/ directory) that defines dependency interfaces and providers. Use dependency containers or context managers to manage lifecycle. This allows easier testing via mock dependencies and clearer dependency contracts.

findings.title: Hardcoded configuration scattered across backend-core and routes
findings.description: Backend configuration exists in backend/app/core/config.py (119 LOC), but there's evidence of potential hardcoded values in route handlers, security module, and database initialization. No single source of truth for feature flags, validation rules, or constants. Makes configuration-driven behavior difficult.

locations.snippet: Centralized config but may have scattered overrides in routes
JWT settings may be hardcoded rather than config-driven

findings.suggested_fix: Audit all Python files for hardcoded values (timeouts, token expiry, page sizes, validation lengths). Move all configuration to backend/app/core/config.py with proper typing and validation using Pydantic Settings. Create environment-specific config overrides (dev.py, test.py, prod.py) if needed. Reference config in routes and services, never hardcode values.

findings.title: Frontend hooks lack clear organizational boundaries
findings.description: Frontend-hooks module (150 LOC, 4 files) contains useAuth, useCustomToast, useMobile, useCopyToClipboard. These are mixed concerns - authentication state, UI notifications, responsive design detection, and clipboard utilities. As the frontend grows, this directory will become a dumping ground. No clear categorization by domain or concern.

locations.snippet: Authentication logic
Toast notification helper
Responsive design detection

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize hooks into subdirectories by concern: frontend/src/hooks/auth/ (useAuth), frontend/src/hooks/ui/ (useCustomToast, useMobile), frontend/src/hooks/utils/ (useCopyToClipboard). As the app grows, add frontend/src/hooks/queries/ for React Query hooks, frontend/src/hooks/mutations/ for mutation hooks.

findings.title: Frontend test utilities mixed with E2E tests
findings.description: Frontend-tests module (400 LOC) mixes Playwright E2E tests (login.spec.ts, admin.spec.ts) with utility functions (tests/utils/user.ts, mailcatcher.ts, random.ts). No clear separation between test specs and shared test infrastructure. As test count grows, this structure won't scale.

locations.snippet: E2E tests mixed with utilities in same directory

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize as: frontend/tests/specs/ for test files, frontend/tests/fixtures/ for test data, frontend/tests/helpers/ for utility functions. Consider frontend/tests/api/ for API helper utilities (privateApi.ts), frontend/tests/services/ for higher-level test orchestration (mailcatcher interactions).

findings.title: Missing interface definitions for frontend-backend contract
findings.description: While frontend-client contains generated OpenAPI types (types.gen.ts, schemas.gen.ts), there's no documented API contract layer or validation schema repository. Changes to backend API schemas require regeneration; no clear versioning or deprecation strategy. Frontend components assume API contract without explicit validation.

locations.snippet: Generated types without explicit documentation
Generated schemas

findings.suggested_fix: Create a frontend/src/types/ directory with documented API contract interfaces that reference generated types. Document API assumptions and breaking change procedures. Consider creating a shared frontend/docs/api-contract.md file. Add API versioning to the backend (v1/v2) if major changes are anticipated. Establish a schema registry or OpenAPI versioning strategy.
